briefs.headline: Wembanyama's 30 points and 14 rebounds carry Spurs past Kings 124-109
briefs.summary: San Antonio scored 75 in the first half, led by 19 at the break and by 24 in the fourth for a seventh straight win in the NBA Cup game at Sacramento; Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Dylan Harper scored 19 apiece. The Spurs, with seven wins and two losses, play at Portland tonight at 10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Alonso backs Palmer and may have Martinez back for Chelsea at Sunderland
briefs.summary: Xabi Alonso said he is "very happy" with Cole Palmer's quality and attitude after England left him out; goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, ahead of schedule after jaw surgery, could return in a mask Sunday at 9 a.m. ET, and Moises Caicedo faces a fitness test for what Alonso called a discomfort rather than his calf.

briefs.headline: De Zerbi says Williams-Barnett, 18, is ready to start for Tottenham
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi said the teenager, who dribbled past three Palace defenders as a substitute last Saturday in his first Premier League appearance, "can play from the beginning" and was considered for the XI at Stamford Bridge last month. Tottenham play at Leeds this morning at 7:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Iraola says Liverpool are 'sometimes too honest' after penalty dispute
briefs.summary: Andoni Iraola questioned the pull on Alexander Isak that went unpunished in last weekend's home defeat to Arsenal and cited Opta's figure that 58% of fouls in Liverpool's games have gone against them; Liverpool, on their first two-match losing run under him, visit Crystal Palace Sunday at 9 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Monken names Sanders the Browns' starter at New Orleans
briefs.summary: Shedeur Sanders makes his first start of the season Sunday at 1 p.m. ET with Deshaun Watson, listed questionable, still in the concussion protocol; as a rookie Sanders won three of seven starts with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Dillon Gabriel could back him up, Monken said Friday.

briefs.headline: Bengals list Dugger out for the Madrid game against the Falcons
briefs.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) is out on ESPN's game page as of Friday night and defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle) is questionable; Jordan Battle, questionable Thursday, is no longer listed. Kickoff at the Bernabeu is Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET, and Atlanta's Brian Robinson Jr. is out.

briefs.headline: Crew need a win and help, FC Cincinnati a win, to skip the Wild Card round
briefs.summary: MLS says Columbus, on 44 points, must win at Chicago and get results elsewhere to avoid the Wild Card round, while FC Cincinnati, on 46, clinch a Round One place by beating Nashville, who need only a draw at TQL Stadium for a single-season points record. Both kick off at 4 p.m. ET on Apple TV.

briefs.headline: Kyushu basho draws a record 2,637 kensho, with Onosato first at 224
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association said Saturday the 15 days of the basho (tournament) opening Sunday in Fukuoka drew 2,637 kensho (sponsor prize banners), past last year's Kyushu record of 2,177; yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato leads with 224, local komusubi Yoshinofuji has 175 and ozeki Aonishiki 128. Hoshoryu, who entered late, has 44.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu opens Sunday against Churanoumi, Onosato against Yoshinofuji
briefs.summary: The JSA's day 1 card, posted Saturday, puts yokozuna Hoshoryu, back from three tournaments out, against a komusubi he has beaten in all six meetings, and Onosato against Yoshinofuji, who has won four of five between them; judging chief Asakayama said that "having entered, there are no excuses." Tickets for all 15 days sold out in about 50 minutes.

briefs.headline: Doncic scores 53 as the Lakers beat Portland 124-118 a night before the Spurs visit
briefs.summary: Luka Doncic's fourth straight 40-point game, a Lakers feat shared only with Baylor, Bryant and Mikan, pushed his average to 40.1; Los Angeles erased a 16-point deficit with 17 straight third-quarter points. Portland, with six wins and two losses, hosts San Antonio tonight.

briefs.headline: Mitchell's career-high 35 lead the Thunder past Memphis 128-97
briefs.summary: Ajay Mitchell and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (28) led Oklahoma City to a 16th straight win over the Grizzlies, who shot 22% from three; the Thunder turned 18 turnovers into 30 points and led by 32 in the third quarter.

briefs.headline: Tatum's 34 send the Celtics past the Hornets 119-80 in NBA Cup play
briefs.summary: Boston made 17 of 31 threes in the first half for a 31-point lead and has won seven of eight; Charlotte, without Kon Knueppel and Moussa Diabate and with Brandon Miller leaving with a groin injury, has lost six straight since Naz Reid's benching.

briefs.headline: Arizona recovers an onside pooch kick and beats TCU 29-28 in the Big 12
briefs.summary: Michael Salgado-Medina's 37-yard field goal with 39 seconds left won it after Zuri Watson recovered the kick at the TCU 26; No. 24 Arizona (7-2, 4-2) kept its Big 12 title hopes alive and TCU (4-5) lost another close one.

briefs.headline: No. 22 New Mexico beats Nevada 31-3 in its first game ever in the AP poll
briefs.summary: Toa Fa'avae led two first-quarter touchdown drives and the Lobos (8-1, 5-0 Mountain West) held Nevada to minus-9 rushing yards and 10 punts; coach Jason Eck's team has three regular-season games left in a playoff chase.

briefs.headline: Illinois beats Nebraska 24-13 and becomes bowl eligible on a fake field goal
briefs.summary: Punter Lars Rau's 29-yard run on a fake set up the go-ahead touchdown; Collin Dixon's two scoring catches gave him a school-record 12 for the season. Illinois (6-3) has won four straight and Nebraska (5-4) has lost four straight.

briefs.headline: Seahawks rule out Darnold and Nelson among six starters against Arizona
briefs.summary: Sam Darnold (quad, cracked rib) and the newly acquired Quenton Nelson, who needs a knee procedure and is week-to-week, will not play Sunday, Mike Macdonald said; Drew Lock starts despite an elbow injury, and Jalen Milroe is the backup.

briefs.headline: Aiyuk meets the 49ers and says he is healthy and seeking reinstatement
briefs.summary: Brandon Aiyuk, who has not played since tearing three knee ligaments in October 2024, met the team for 75 minutes Friday with agent Drew Rosenhaus; the league wants about $13 million in bonus money repaid first, a source told ESPN, and the trade deadline is Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Ducks beat Flames 5-3, the first team since 1992 to score five in seven straight
briefs.summary: Cutter Gauthier's goal with 1:34 left extended his streak to five games and 10 goals; Anaheim is the first team since the 1991-92 Penguins with at least five goals in seven consecutive games, and Jackson LaCombe's nine-game points streak is a franchise record for a defenseman.

briefs.headline: Kaprizov's NHL-leading 16th goal and three assists carry the Wild past the Sharks 4-1
briefs.summary: Minnesota has 27 points, the most in the Western Conference, and is 6-0-1 in its last seven; Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 shots for his 11th win in 16 starts, both NHL bests among goalies.

briefs.headline: Bettor testifies Clase pitch tips dried up after the Mizuhara scandal
briefs.summary: Luis de Aza Baez, a government witness who has agreed to forfeit $69,000, said he bet on Clase pitch velocities in 2023 on tips relayed through a group chat and was told in 2024 there was no more information; the Brooklyn trial resumes Thursday.

briefs.headline: Diamondbacks' Carroll has elbow surgery, expected back for spring training
briefs.summary: Arizona confirmed Friday that Corbin Carroll, 26, had loose bodies removed from his right elbow this week, with recovery put at about eight weeks; the three-time All-Star hit .239 with 22 homers and a league-high 17 triples and won his first Gold Glove.

briefs.headline: Barry's brace lifts Everton past Coventry 3-1 and into the top five
briefs.summary: Thierno Barry came from behind to score twice after Yann Gboho's opener and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added the third in the 81st minute; Everton have won three straight, and David Moyes equalled Harry Catterick's club record of 592 matches in charge.

waters.reading: 57.5 cfs, 1.36 feet at 5:15 a.m., steady on both against 56.2 cfs and 1.35 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Friday's edition reading of 56.2 cfs and 1.35 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is up 1.3 cfs and 0.01 feet on the day, a second straight morning not down after 19 falling ones, and this time the trace shows a real bump rather than a flicker: the USGS record climbed from 56.2 at 5 a.m. Friday to 57.5 at 6:30, 58.8 at 9:30, 60.1 at 12:30 p.m. and 61.5 from 2 to 5 p.m., then fell back through 60.1 at 6:30, 58.8 at 11 p.m. and 57.5 from 3:30 a.m. on, the stage topping at 1.39 and settling at 1.36. Five cfs up and four back down inside 24 hours is a shower on the headwaters or a cloud passing over the gauge's sun, and the trace does not say which; the daily mean for Friday was 58.8 cfs against 55.6 Thursday and 55.5 Wednesday, so the recession's floor has moved up a notch, from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 and 653 on Oct. 17 through 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31 to this week's high 50s. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "58 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's fish-stocking page, fetched this morning, again carries an empty list under the waters stocked, and the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is still Oct. 29. At 58 cfs and clear the Williams is still the file's low-water problem, two cfs of bump notwithstanding: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the middle of an overcast day, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, and a four-cfs bump is not it.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.95 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.38 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.9 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool rising, 0.57 over its 24.38 comparison point, but that point is Thursday morning's drawdown, not Friday's; against Friday's edition reading of 25.02 at 5 a.m. the pool is down 0.07 on the day, and the rise is the last half hour. Friday's trace held 24.99 to 25.02 through the morning, eased to 24.93 at 2 p.m., 24.86 at 5 p.m. and 24.75 at 8 p.m., sat between 24.82 and 24.84 from 9:30 p.m. to 3:30 a.m., then went 24.80 at 4:30, 24.86 at 4:45 and 24.95 at 5 a.m., 0.15 in half an hour with no rain in the bucket, which is the dam moving water, not the hills. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.9 the gauge is two feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool that has done nothing but breathe a quarter of a foot in a day fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling into November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. The half-hour uptick at 5 a.m. says the pool is being topped up at daybreak, which puts a little pull back through the wing dams for the first hour of light.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.19 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.29 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.2 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge steady, 0.10 under its 26.29 comparison point, which is Thursday's 5 a.m. value and not Friday's; against Friday's edition reading of 26.17 at 5 a.m. it is up 0.02 on the day, and the day in between was a slow climb and a sawtooth: the trace rose from 26.14 at 6:30 a.m. Friday to 26.34 at 9:30, 26.40 at 2 p.m. and a 26.47 high at 3:30 p.m., then ran between 26.25 and 26.39 through the evening, dipped to 26.03 at 3:30 a.m. and came back to 26.19 at 5 a.m. The dam below tells the rest: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge jumping from 22,100 cfs at 5 a.m. Friday to 31,400 at 6:30 a.m., settling to 23,000 to 25,300 through the afternoon, rising again to a 35,900 peak at 10:45 p.m. and falling to 22,500 at 5 a.m. Saturday, the Ironton stage 34.43 to 34.59 and back to 34.41 at the same points. So Thursday night's drain-and-recover did not repeat in any form: with Greenup passing more water through the night than it had all day, the Huntington reach held within a third of a foot and the Byrd pool above held flat. Whether the pattern is scheduled or a lockage rhythm the traces still do not say, and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach is a tenth higher than Friday morning with Greenup drawing 22,000 cfs below, so there is push on the seams this morning, and the fishing goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, which feed better with the push on, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 12:14 AM at 0.3 ft, high 6:20 AM at 4.2 ft, low 12:54 PM at 0.6 ft, high 6:35 PM at 3.6 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 5:39 AM at 5.4 ft, low 11:58 AM at 0.3 ft, high 5:55 PM at 4.3 ft, low 11:47 PM at 0.2 ft. Water 68.2F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon a waning crescent, 7% illuminated, 27.1 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 6:20 AM and 6:35 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day for once, the 12:14 a.m. low already behind us at press time; the sound lags the surf 41 minutes on the morning high, 56 on the midday low and 40 on the evening high, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes, and the surf's 11:47 p.m. low reaches the sound after midnight, on Sunday's table. The ranges are the biggest of the week and still building: a 3.9-foot fill overnight from 0.3 to this morning's 4.2, a 3.6-foot drain to 12:54 p.m., a 3.0-foot fill to 6:35 p.m., the morning sound high 4.2 against Friday's 4.1 and the surf high 5.4 against 5.2, with the moon at 7% and the new moon about Monday, so these are spring tides and the inlet will run hard either side of slack. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 68.2F, up 0.7 on Friday's 67.5, a fourth straight morning of warming. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is six days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier with scattered speckled trout starting to show, night bottom fishing producing good-sized Virginia mullet and spot, and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel very good before the wind; East Coast Sports with the piers catching big red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and the occasional trout inside, and trout to dominate as it cools; Native Son with cooler evenings pushing trout into the creeks, the five- to eight-foot seams the depth to look, and reds inside taking cut bait over artificials; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many small specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water, black drum to 18 inches and small reds on the same floated shrimp, and a 3/16-ounce jighead with a Slick Jr. for the artificial; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds on the oyster and grass banks on soft plastics; and the boats with kings in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on the nearshore structure, sea bass and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS Wilmington product was active for coastal Pender or New Hanover, the Topsail point or the adjacent marine zones at 5:50 a.m. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it is a flood tide at press time: the sound tops out at 6:20 a.m. and then drains for six and a half hours to the 12:54 p.m. low, the biggest morning ebb of the week on a spring tide. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the flooded grass edges in the first hour of light around the 6:20 a.m. high, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through mid-morning, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after 1 p.m. and again either side of the 6:35 p.m. high. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 10:30 a.m. to the 12:54 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high at 6:35 p.m. puts drum up on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights until the next low after midnight, the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
